name: Protein-yogurt pizza pittas — no-yeast (base pitta, pre-filling)

source.author: Instagram — shirel_blank / foodsdictionary_recipes (Hebrew caption)
source.notes: Quick no-yeast / no-rise pittas from a protein-yogurt dough, pan-fried and stuffed pizza-style. Analyzed PER PITTA for the DOUGH BASE ONLY (pre-filling) — makes 8-9 pittas; per-unit values use 8. The filling (pizza sauce, grated yellow/mozzarella cheese, 'toppings you like') is unquantified in the caption and is NOT included in these macros — see the filling note. PRO yogurt taken as a ~20 g-protein/200 g protein yogurt.

serving_desc: 1 pitta (~62 g cooked) — recipe makes 8-9; base only, no filling

ingredients.item: FILLING (not in macros): grated yellow cheese / mozzarella
ingredients.note: adds calcium + sat fat + sodium — the main add-on cost

ingredients.item: FILLING (not in macros): toppings you like

steps: Mix all dough ingredients to a uniform dough; rest, roll, stuff with sauce + cheese, pan-fry both sides.

batch_totals.note: Base dough only (8 pittas). Filling adds calories/fat/sodium on top depending on how much sauce + cheese you use.

him.verdict: A better-than-average bread base: the protein yogurt lifts each pitta to ~5.6 g protein for 157 kcal — more than a plain pitta (~3-4 g) — with a bit of olive-oil fat. But it's refined white flour, so low fiber (~0.8 g) and mostly fast carbs. As a controlled higher-protein carb/bread swap it's fine; it's a vehicle, not a protein source. Watch the FILLING — that's where the cheese piles on calories, saturated fat and sodium (unquantified here).
flags: higher protein than normal bread (~5.6 g/pitta from the yogurt)
refined white flour, low fiber (~0.8 g)
filling (cheese/sauce) is the real calorie/sodium lever
suggested_mods: Swap half the white flour for whole-wheat to add fiber + folate
Go light on the yellow cheese in the filling — biggest calorie/sat-fat/sodium add
Load veg toppings and use the tomato pizza sauce (lycopene) to make it more of a meal

her_preconception.verdict: The base is a refined-flour bread — not a nutrient contributor, though the protein yogurt adds a little protein and calcium. Fully cooked, pasteurized yogurt, no safety flags. Whole-wheat flour would add the folate/fiber it's missing. When filled, keep cheese pasteurized (standard) and toppings cooked.
prenatal_highlights: a little protein + calcium from the yogurt
suggested_mods: Use whole-wheat or half-whole-wheat flour to add folate + fiber
Pair with a protein + veg filling to make it prenatally useful

cooking_guide: In a bowl, mix the flour, baking powder and salt, then add the yogurt, olive oil and cold water. Stir to a shaggy dough, then knead ~1-2 min just until smooth — don't overwork it (over-kneading makes tough pittas).
Cover and rest the dough 10-15 min — this lets the flour hydrate and the gluten relax, so it rolls out easily and cooks up soft.
Divide into 8-9 balls. On a floured surface, roll each ~½ cm thick (thin enough to cook through, thick enough to stay fluffy).
For the pizza version: spread a little pizza sauce and cheese on one half, fold over (or top a second round) and press the edges to seal.

Heat a pan over medium with a thin film of olive oil. Cook each pitta ~2-3 min per side until deep golden with brown spots and the cheese is melted — medium heat, not high, so the inside cooks before the outside burns.
Keep the finished pittas under a clean towel so they stay soft.
Tip: no yeast means no rise time, but the 10-15 min rest is what keeps them tender — don't skip it.
